title: The Abbey of St. Mary in the Valley of Jehoshaphat, Jerusalem
author: C. N. Johns
location_note: Municipal sewer trench in the Kidron Valley within 50 m west of the Church of the Tomb of the Virgin, Jerusalem; no map reference; placed by name.
reading: p. 117 in full; then eligible-class keyword passages (pp. 118-136), with the pavement, drain and press passages read in full
notes: Summer 1937 sewer trench: Crusader pavements, walls and a cruciform pier of the 12th-c. abbey; lower late-Byzantine mosaic floors with a re-used 6th-c. tombstone ('Tomb of Kasios and Adios', not a burial feature). Cisterns named only in a 12th-c. pilgrim text (not coded). The crypt of the Tomb of the Virgin is the known church, not a new feature.

features.site: abbey courtyard (L-K) and ranges EF, K
features.subtype: built stone-covered drain canalizing the Kidron torrent under the pavement; plastered side drain; earthenware pipe drain in a cross-wall
features.quote: Like the later sewer, this drain canalized the torrent of the valley

features.subtype: rectangular emplacement in a lime-ash floor, 'perhaps ... connected with a press' (possible oil- or wine-press outhouse)
features.quote: perhaps a piece of machinery connected with a press
